title: Databases
statusUnavailable: The panel could not read the state of the database servers.

unsupported.platform: Databases are not available on this distribution yet.

empty.title: No database server installed
empty.text: Install MariaDB or MySQL, PostgreSQL, or Redis or Valkey on the software page; they then appear here.

unmanaged: Installed but not managed by the panel on this system yet: {names}.
noCluster: This PostgreSQL version was installed without its main cluster, so it has no databases yet.

remote.enableRestart: The server will listen on every address instead of only locally. This restarts the service (it needs systemd), so open connections are dropped.
remote.enablePg: PostgreSQL will listen on every address. Users still need hosts that allow their remote address.
remote.disable: The server will listen locally only; remote clients can no longer connect.
remote.firewallNote: Remote access is on: clients on other machines also need port {port} opened on the Firewall page.

hints.mysqlName: Letters, digits and _, up to 64 characters.
hints.mysqlUser: Letters, digits and _, up to 32 characters.
hints.pgName: Lower-case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter or _, up to 63 characters.
hints.keep: Leave empty to keep the current one
hints.hosts: Where the user may connect from: localhost, % (anywhere), an IPv4 address or a CIDR range. Leave empty for local only.
hints.pgHosts: Local connections are always allowed; hosts add remote ones (an IPv4 address or a CIDR range).

db.withUser: Also create a user for it
db.dropContent: The database and all its data are deleted. This cannot be undone.
db.emptyText: Create a database; a user of the same name can be created with it.
db.withUserHint: A user with full access to it, named like the database unless you name it below.

steps.user: Create user {user} with full access to it
steps.userGenerated: Create user {user} with full access to it and a generated password
steps.local: Let the user connect from this server only

user.dropContent: Programs that sign in as this user will no longer be able to connect.

grant.none: No access to any database yet.

password.title: Password of {name}
password.hint: Copy it now; it is not kept on this page after you close the dialog.

dumps.intro: Dumps are kept on this server. Download them to keep a copy elsewhere.
dumps.redisIntro: Snapshots are copies of the Redis data file (RDB), kept on this server.
dumps.deleteContent: The dump file is deleted from this server.
dumps.badName: Only .sql and .sql.gz files (and .dump for PostgreSQL) can be uploaded, with a name of letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.

restore.title: Restore a dump
restore.userHint: Restoring runs as the owner, or as a user with full access to the database whose password the panel knows.
restore.intro: The dump is loaded into an existing database.
restore.warning: Objects in the dump replace the ones in the database with the same names.
restore.needsUser: Create the database through the panel (it then has a known owner), or give a user whose password the panel knows full access to it.

steps.asOwner: Run it as the owner of the database

redis.removeRemote: Remote access is on; Redis refuses it without a password.
redis.maxMemoryHint: 0 means no limit. When the limit is reached, the eviction policy decides what happens.
redis.persistenceHint: Without persistence, the data is lost when Redis restarts.

keys.intro: Choose a database number and a pattern, then scan.
keys.truncated: Only the first part of the value is shown.
keys.deleteContent: The keys and their values are deleted from {db}.

service.stopText: Sites and apps that use {name} lose their connection until it is started again.
